Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. item.title: Asheville Jazz Orchestra Labor Day Show — Mon Sep 7, 2:00 PM — Highland Brewing
item.description:
Kick back, sip one of your favorite local brews, and soak in the mountain air as the Asheville Jazz Orchestra brings the sound of big band to Highland Brewing! From vintage swing-era classics to bold, modern big band sounds, the AJO keeps things groovin’ with music that’s fun, free, and made for all ages.
The AJO is an 18 piece jazz band featuring vocalist Wendy Jones. Expect styles ranging from Classic Big Band of the 1940’s to modern songs written by band members! Hot soloists and a tight band that is soooo much fun to dance to!
Bring a chair, bring your peeps, and get ready for an afternoon of good vibes, great tunes, and the kind of community spirit that makes Asheville feel like home. Free Show • Family-Friendly • All Are Welcome

item.title: Spartanburg: Campuses, Downtown, and a Traditional Stop at Krispy Kreme — Sat Sep 12, 8:30 AM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group We will join the Asheville Amblers, AARP, and perhaps some others, for a delightful walk through picturesque "Sparkle City" with its many beautiful fountains. The walk includes Converse and Wofford Colleges and Liberty Park, tree-lined neighborhoods, fine homes, and a vibrant downtown.
Choices are between a 6 KM/3.7 mile, a 9 KM/ 5.6 mile, and a 12 KM/7.5 mile walk. The latter two include the traditional stop at the Krispy Kreme across the street from the location of the historic, original Krispy Kreme store.
Look for us in the break room at the YMCA of Greater Spartanburg. Register at 8:30. Step-off at 9:00. (The walk is free, but the Amblers do accept donations; suggested donation is $4.00).

item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Sep 27, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

item.title: In Conversation | An Artist Talk by Lesley Dill — Tue Oct 6, 6:00 PM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Join us for an evening with New York-based artist Lesley Dill, whose work is featured in the current exhibition, The Art of Paper. Dill will talk about her projects that involve paper and collaboration, from huge community and large-scale installations to the intimate creation of artist books and sculptures, as well as her work with artists, poets, students, and studios, such as Tamarind and Dieu Donne. PAPER IS MY FRIEND: “Paper is about fingertip energy for me. The way one moves in to touch paper is like no other approach. It’s as if each finger has a little imaginary rocketship in it. We touch nothing else the way we touch paper. Paper is the medium of intimacy. The end result is wonder. All printmaking begins with the choice of what paper and in this way, it is about a relationship to fragility and force. item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Oct 31, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

A post shared by Uncle Paul (@unclepaul.music)

Don't worry if you can't make this one, though! It’s a monthly event; you'll have plenty of chances to get your pie on :)
